A minor addendum.

It has always been true that a few people had... Minor concerns about these 'helpful spirits.' Not everyone likes their underwear reorganized. Some are quick to mistrust such influence. Among those, there is demand for these new goods that ward off the 'spirits.' Not always were these the sorts to like chaos, nor always the sorts that had crimes worth hiding. Some people merely don't like the idea of invisible spirits in their house; Or have (largely mistakenly) blamed them for things going wrong in their lives, as pattern-seeking sentients are prone to mis-attribute; Or simply have string ideas of property, particular notions of who does and does not belong in their house uninvited.

Not especially many. But such people exist.

Somewhere, a man preaches that these spirits are surely evil, and that homes must be warded off from their influence. People don't, largely, believe this particular preacher; He raises money by selling warding-herbs, after all, and that is an easy motive to mistrust. Perhaps there will be more such preachers in the future - people like a good firey sermon about the evils of something-or-other. Perhaps not.

Elsewhere, people have been living keeper-less for some time. Perhaps they came from messy families, but for some reason or other, 'helpful cleaning spirits' are just not something in their worldview. Orchids come, orchids go, and little mind is paid to their status one way or the other. The difference is that now even orderly children of some messy families may not know of Keepers, due to happening to live where they may now no longer tread. And so, in the future, there are liable to be places in the world where 'helpful cleaning spirits' are not something known. Perhaps, people from such places, upon traveling, will find themselves delighted and pleased that such spirits exist; Perhaps, they will find them odd and suspicious, a weird magic those 'other folk' have that 'honest folk don't truck with.' Surely there will be some in either camp, depending, in part, on how crotchety they and their parents are.

[m] Just expanding on the motives of people who cultivate this stuff. They're not all into the idea of 'chaos brew' and 'screw order' - people are complicated, and prone to being mistaken, mistrustful, stupid, ignorant, or unlucky enough to have ideas about the world that would not occur to those that know what's going on.

The knowledge of the Orchids begins to spread easily enough. But it has competition.

Wild rumors spring up seemingly out of nowhere, seemingly taking on lives of their own. Everywhere, sentients are claiming different things repel or attract the cleaning spirits, occasionally claiming knowledge from the spirits themselves.

The orchids have the advantage of truth. But the rumors are wily, and powerful. And evolving.

Argondal has found his forge devoid of spirits since he has left orchids inside. He hears rumors (which are quickly spreading) about how Orchids repel these Keepers. Superstitions have begun to spread, including rumors of other things repelling and attracting spirit. Similarly, polarizing opinions begin forming about the Keepers. Argondal removes the orchids and begins destroying roots, and receives a blade for every root.
